title: @c15t/backend: Self-Hosted Consent Backend
description: Run the c15t consent backend on your own server and database. It resolves consent policies, stores consent records and audit history, and serves every c15t frontend through one web `Request` handler.
features: You own the data: consent records stay in your PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite database
Policy rules by region, with presets such as `policyRulePresets.europeOptIn()`
One web-standard `Request` to `Response` handler that mounts in Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, TanStack Start, or any server
Geolocation from host headers, server-side translations, and audit logs
IAB TCF configuration with the Global Vendor List and custom vendors
The same API as Inth, so frontends change only the backend URL
prerequisites: A PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite database, plus its driver: `@effect/sql-pg`, `@effect/sql-mysql2`, or `@effect/sql-sqlite-node`
A server that runs Node.js. A static export cannot run the backend
manualInstallation: Install the driver version that the backend lists as a peer dependency. Do not want to run a database? [Inth](https://inth.com) runs this backend for you.
usage: Create `c15t-backend.config.ts` with your database, trusted origins, and policy rules
Create the schema: `npx @c15t/cli self-host migrate --config ./c15t-backend.config.ts --plan`, then run it again with `--apply`
Mount the handler on a catch-all route for `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `OPTIONS`

```ts
// app/api/c15t/[[...path]]/route.ts (Next.js)
import { c15tInstance } from '@c15t/backend'

import config from '../../../../c15t-backend.config'

export const runtime = 'nodejs'
const backend = c15tInstance({ ...config, basePath: '/api/c15t' })

export const GET = (request: Request) => backend.handler(request)
export const POST = GET
export const PUT = GET
export const PATCH = GET
export const OPTIONS = GET
```
Point your frontend at the backend URL, such as `https://app.example.com/api/c15t`, where the quickstart asks for the Inth URL
For other servers, PostgreSQL, and deployment checks, see the [self-hosting guide](https://c15t.com/docs/self-host/quickstart)

customSections.Hosted or Self-Hosted:
Self-host when you need to run the service and its database yourself. You then own provisioning, migrations, backups, policy configuration, signing secrets, availability, and upgrades.

[Inth](https://inth.com) runs the same backend for you, with a dashboard, audit history, and a managed IAB CMP ID. Your frontend code is the same either way.
